subject: Estimates of N between sessions where Sex variable is involved.

messages.author: f4c3467fbe3bbbec
messages.subject: Estimates of N between sessions where Sex variable is involved.
parts:
Hi All,

Apologies for what may be quite a trivial question - I am struggling to find an answer in the literature and decided it's time to call in the brains trust!

I have built the following non-spatial capture-recapture model in openCR in an effort to estimate N (local population estimate) for each of my 9 sessions.

surv_base_model_NS_basic5 <- openCR.fit(DI_capthist_CJS_2,
                                        details = list(fastproximity = FALSE, control = list(maxit = 5000)), 
                                        type="JSSAN",
                                        method = "Nelder-Mead",
                                        start=list(p=0.5, phi=0.5, N=10),
                                        model=list(p~Sex, phi~Sex, N~t))

Notably, in this model I have allowed p and phi to vary by Sex, and N by Session.
The 'predict' function applied to my model object: 'predict(surv_base_model_NS_basic5)' gives me estimates of N for each session while holding Sex constant as female. 

$N session Sex estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl 1 1 F 8.956276 3.348190 4.304440 18.63538 2 2 F 14.564573 4.699008 7.738776 27.41090 3 3 F 11.795131 3.392508 6.712445 20.72644 4 4 F 20.827266 4.533467 13.594128 31.90900 5 5 F 18.916916 3.975262 12.530721 28.55779 6 7 F 6.100102 1.813744 3.406036 10.92509 7 8 F 13.863956 3.734179 8.177504 23.50464 8 9 F 12.950964 3.559051 7.557596 22.19323 9 10 F 8.379221 2.843470 4.308741 16.29510

If I provide 'newdata' to the 'predict' function, specifying both M and F for each session, it gives me the same estimate for both sexes at each session:

$N session Sex estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl 1 1 F 8.956276 3.348190 4.304440 18.63538 2 1 F 14.564573 4.699008 7.738776 27.41090 3 1 F 11.795131 3.392508 6.712445 20.72644 4 1 F 20.827266 4.533467 13.594128 31.90900 5 1 F 18.916916 3.975262 12.530721 28.55779 6 1 F 6.100102 1.813744 3.406036 10.92509 7 1 F 13.863956 3.734179 8.177504 23.50464 8 1 F 12.950964 3.559051 7.557596 22.19323 9 1 F 8.379221 2.843470 4.308741 16.29510 10 1 M 8.956276 3.348190 4.304440 18.63538 11 1 M 14.564573 4.699008 7.738776 27.41090 12 1 M 11.795131 3.392508 6.712445 20.72644 13 1 M 20.827266 4.533467 13.594128 31.90900 14 1 M 18.916916 3.975262 12.530721 28.55779 15 1 M 6.100102 1.813744 3.406036 10.92509 16 1 M 13.863956 3.734179 8.177504 23.50464 17 1 M 12.950964 3.559051 7.557596 22.19323 18 1 M 8.379221 2.843470 4.308741 16.29510 Can I use the estimate from the first example (where Sex is held constant) as my N, or do I need to multiply this by 2 to account for both sexes (i.e., adding up the predictions for both males and females in the second example)?
 Sincere thanks in advance for any help! Tash

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Estimates of N between sessions where Sex variable is involved.
parts:
Not a trivial question. I don't think openCR will give you a sex-specific N that way. Also, there are no groups in openCR so that MARK-like route is not available. openCR _does_ have a stratification option for spatial analyses that happens also to work in this non-spatial case (below). It's very slow to fit for reasons I haven't investigated. You are much better to just split the sexes if there are no shared parameters. 'fastproximity' is not a 'details' argument  in openCR.
Murray

library(openCR)

# try with dipper data
fitN <- openCR.fit(dipperCH,
                   type = "JSSAN",
                   model = list(p~sex, phi~sex, N~t))

# restructure data
dipperCHsex <- stratify(dipperCH, covariate = 'sex')

# split sexes, as all parameters sex-specific
fitNF <- openCR.fit(dipperCHsex[['Female']], type = "JSSAN", model = list(N~t))
fitNM <- openCR.fit(dipperCHsex[['Male']], type = "JSSAN", model = list(N~t))

predict(fitNF)$N
predict(fitNM)$N

# or stratify model by sex (slow!)
fitN.st <- openCR.fit(dipperCHsex, stratified = TRUE,
                      type = "JSSAN",
                      start = fitN,   # use fast model for starting values
                      model = list(p~stratum, phi~stratum, N~t*stratum))
predict(fitN.st)$N
